page: Amazon Web Services c8id.96xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor with 192 physical cores and 384 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The system is equipped with 768.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 7 GHz, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage consists of 22,800 GB of NVMe SSD instance store volumes, and the instance supports a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps.

In multi-core processing benchmarks, the instance achieves top-tier performance, ranking in the top 10% for stress-ng multi-core CPU tests, PassMark CPU scores, and software compilation. The Intel Xeon processor includes Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), which contribute to top-tier scores in CPU encryption and physics simulations. Memory bandwidth is also highly rated, with read-only and write-only large block transfers placing in the top 10%. However, single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core results falling in the middle 50%.

While prompt processing for large language models ranks in the top 25%, text generation speeds are a notable bottleneck, dropping to the bottom 10% for small models and middle 50% for larger models due to the absence of dedicated GPU hardware. The instance is highly efficient for workloads that leverage its massive parallel compute capacity and high-speed local NVMe storage, such as database operations, Redis deployments, and static web serving, where it achieves top-tier throughput. It is less suited for tasks requiring high single-threaded performance or real-time LLM text generation.
description: Amazon Web Services c8id.96xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized instance featuring 384 vCPUs and 192 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at 3.9 GHz. It is equipped with 768.0 GB of DDR5 memory at 7 GHz and 22,800 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, alongside a 100 Gbps baseline network. Benchmark results indicate top-tier performance in multi-core CPU execution, memory bandwidth, and database operations, supported by hardware-accelerated instruction sets like AVX-512 and AMX. However, single-core performance is average, and LLM text generation speeds are limited by the absence of dedicated GPUs. This instance is best suited for highly parallelized workloads, large-scale database operations, high-throughput web serving, and software compilation.
